body.statement: For every \(p_{\circ}\in(0,1)\), the \((X,Z)\)-marginal of \(P^{\circ}\) is absolutely continuous with density bounded and strictly positive on each of its two support rectangles, while observed outcomes are bounded, exact stayers have probability zero, and marginal quasi-stayers exist. Conditional quasi-stayer support fails for every \(x\in[-1,0)\), a baseline region of probability \(p_{\circ}\). The observed objects are \(X_0=[-1,1]\), \(H=[-1,0]\times[1/2,1]\cup[0,1]\times[-1/4,1/4]\), \(g=0\), \(A=(1+5p_{\circ})/8\), \(T=0\), and \(d\nu_P(x)=p_{\circ}\mathbf 1\{x\in[-1,0]\}dx\). The obstacle envelopes equal \(r_P(x)=-\ell_P(x)=\min\{-x,1/2\}\) on \([-1,0]\) and vanish on \([0,1]\), yielding \(\Theta(P^{\circ})=[-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ}),3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})]\). The displayed affine laws \(Q_+^{\circ}\) and \(Q_-^{\circ}\) both belong to the continuous-trend legal completion class, preserve the entire observed law, and satisfy parallel trends on the baseline-treatment support and the stronger all-\(I\) equality because their period differences are respectively \(u_+^{\circ}(X)\) and \(u_-^{\circ}(X)\) at every dose. They satisfy the new conditional mean-movement bound and attain respectively \(-3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\) and \(3p_{\circ}/(1+5p_{\circ})\).
body.justification: The positive-density family proves that the conditional-support failure and non-singleton frontier persist away from atomic examples, while the two schedules display legal full-law attainment.
body.gap: The public conditional-quasi-stayer theorem covers the nested singleton regime, and the common-zero-baseline result has scalar geometry; neither supplies an absolutely continuous heterogeneous-baseline support-hole family with two observed-law-equivalent WAOSS values.
body.consumer: The family is a regular stress test for support diagnostics, obstacle solvers, and sensitivity plots indexed by the mass \(p_{\circ}\) of unsupported baselines.
